course_summary:
ISEN 609 | Probability for Engineering Decisions | Fall 2026
Instructor: Petar Momcilovic | petar@tamu.edu
Meets: R 5:30PM-8:30PM | ZACH 211
Grading: Assignments [20%], First exam [40%], Second exam [40%] — A: 90-100%, B: 80-89%, C: 70-79%, D: 60-69%, F: <60%
Topics: Monte Carlo Markov chain, Beyes rule, law of total probability, linearity of expectation, balance equations, value iteration, synthesis of optimal policy, policy iteration, Poisson process, embedded chain, probability spaces, axioms, conditional probability, dependence, random variables, distributions, expectation operator, multivariate distributions, computation of expectations, Discrete-time Markov chains, modeling, transient analysis, classification of states, steady-state analysis, Dynamic programming, finite-horizon problems, infinite-horizon discounted problems, Continuous-time Markov chains, exponential distribution, properties, probability theory, probability, stochastic processes, uncertainty in engineering decisions, algebra, calculus
Tools: Python, R, Matlab
Prerequisites: Approval of instructor, undergraduate course in probability
